# The step of a dot product of one limb: one fused multiply-add

Kernel `dot_step_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: the oracle tests it, but Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

$s + x y$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y).$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Target (not proved)

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y)$: the number of the format nearest to $s + x y$, ties to even.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked.

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition dot_step_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s x y : R,
  fmt emin prec s ->
  fmt emin prec x ->
  fmt emin prec y ->
  let t := dot_step_1 emin prec tie_even s x y in
  fmt emin prec t /\
  t = RN emin prec (s + (x * y)).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** the step of the fused dot product of one limb, s <- RN(x y + s) (milestone2.md). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/dot_step_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/dot_step_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The step of the dot product of one limb (milestone2.md, "sum, dot, axpy, convolution"): one
# fused operation, s <- RN(x y + s). No product is rounded: the step is the addition of the state
# and of the exact product. Its elements come from arrays the program supplies; it only multiplies
# them, so rule R3 asks no guard of them (an entry kernel whose x and y enter from the program).

t = fma(x, y, s)
```
